models_evaluated: machine-learning PrEP prediction model with interactive EHR alerts

links.outcome: New PrEP prescriptions and HIV testing at pilot versus matched control clinics
links.effect: New PrEP prescriptions were 4.5 times higher at pilot clinics (0.09% vs. 0.02%), but the 5.5% increase in HIV tests per 100 patients was not statistically significant.
links.quote: Although numbers of PrEP prescriptions remained low, the proportion of all patients with new PrEP prescriptions was 4.5 times higher at pilot clinics compared with matched control clinics (0.09% vs. 0.02%).

unlisted_practices: Blending data-driven risk identification with providers' traditional decision-making framework and building provider trust to support adoption

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment and implementation of an EHR-integrated predictive risk model alert for HIV PrEP in primary care clinics compared to control clinics, without testing specific deployment safeguard variations.
